decisions.reason: The polymer concrete housing had a dedicated page in both years, which signals substantial tooling investment and visible commitment as a base component within compatible product families, so dropping it would write off sunk costs.

Floor-level shower drainage is central to the firm's announced direction toward accessible, low-profile systems, and its prominence rose to a dedicated page in 2019, so management will persist with it.

Visibility declined from a dedicated page to a mere mention, but design-conscious drainage is part of the firm's stated value proposition, so management can attribute weaker results to temporary causes and keep it, though with elevated risk.

The integrated-slope shower element was only ever mentioned, implying modest public commitment, but it fits the integrated low-profile strategy and supports the floor-level shower system, so it is likely kept with moderate drop risk.
The DallSafe 200 was publicly launched with press-style claims and featured on the home page, a strong visible commitment that management would need to justify, so it will be retained.

The air-admittance valve is peripheral to the core drainage-design strategy and received little visible commitment, making it the easiest to drop, but as a low-cost complementary accessory in a stable portfolio it is still more likely kept.
